title: SDK Sprint Essentials — Pocket Guide (annotated)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, action-first guide for running 1–3 day SDK onboarding sprints with customers or internal teams. Focus is ‘get a running sample + telemetry in 15 minutes’, then expand with three micro-experiments. This is intentionally terse — treat as pocket reference during pairing sessions and field demos.

Audience:
- Developer advocates running live lab sessions
- Solutions engineers onboarding evaluation partners
- New hires in SDK/DevEx doing first integrations

Core outcomes (90–180 minutes):
1) Hello-world sample wired to Redwood API (API key, region, model) and passing tokens through minimal client.
2) Basic telemetry events emitted: request_id, latency_ms, model_name, prompt_hash.
3) One safety/fallback path: local stub + retry/backoff integration.

15-minute ramp checklist (fast path):
- Preflight: ensure account with credit; create API key; pick region (us-west-2).
- Clone minimal repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter && cd sdk-starter/minimal
- Install: pnpm install || pip install -r requirements.txt (note language per audience)
- Configure: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx; export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
- Run smoke: node samples/hello.js OR python samples/hello.py — expect "Hello from Redwood" token stream
- Verify tokens: console output + one telemetry ping in sandbox console

Dev-loop micro-scenarios (next 60–120 min):
A) Prompt shaping: replace sample prompt with domain example; validate model_name and length behavior.
B) Latency-sensitive path: switch to streaming mode; exercise partial response handler.
C) Cost-aware test: enable small-batch generation with short max_tokens and assert cost delta in telemetry.

Instrumentation & telemetry quick rules:
- Minimal event set: request_id, sdk_version, model, region, latency_ms, token_count, success|error, fallback_reason (if any).
- Use consistent keys: telemetry.event_source = "sdk-pocket-sprint"
- Sample code: include synchronous flush before process exit in short demos (common omission).

Common friction and debug notes (notes-to-self style):
- Missing API key -> ambiguous 401 in some SDK versions; update error copy to include "check REDWOOD_API_KEY"
- Local networking issue when streaming behind corp proxy: add env REDWOOD_DISABLE_HTTP2=true as workaround
- Telemetry not appearing: ensure sample uses sandbox telemetry write-key (different from API key)

Canary/cutover snippet idea (for follow-up doc):
- Feature flag flow for model swap: route v1->v2 with 10% canary, watch latency and quality score on small eval set, auto-rollback if latency > baseline + 150ms or quality drop > 5pts.

Lab facilitation tips (for advocates):
- Start with the 15-minute ramp, then pause and ask: "what would you change for your use case?" Use answers to pick one micro-scenario.
- Keep a backup stub server to show deterministic outputs for debugging.
- Encourage attendees to open devtools and watch the streaming chunking — helps explain batching/cost.

Unresolved questions / next tasks (TODO):
- Add language-specific quick patches for Go and Rust (currently JS/Python prioritized).
- Draft a one-page troubleshooting card for network/proxy and telemetry mismatches. Owner: Ravi. Target: next week.
- Add an interactive playground script to auto-generate prompt variants for the prompt-shaping micro-test. Owner: Maya.

References & quick links used in sessions:
- Starter repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-starter/pull/87
- Ticket for canary rollout proto: JIRA:DX-514
- Internal playflows doc: confluence:DX/mini-sprint-playflows

Appendix (scripts & snippets to copy):
- Node streaming listener (one-liner): client.chat.stream({model, messages}).on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d.chunk))
- Python flush example: telemetry.flush(timeout=2) 

Notes-to-self tone: keep it short, with copyable commands. When converting to a public quickstart, split out the telemetry section into a separate "observability primer" and expand code examples per language.

-- end pocket guide --
